title: Sam Walton: listening and cost discipline
principle: Combine customer service with cost discipline and employee feedback.
keyLessons: Walmart publishes Walton rules emphasizing employee participation, communication, listening and customer expectations.

Cost control supports competitive resilience. Application: ask frontline staff about one avoidable expense and test a service-preserving improvement. This adaptation does not establish that every cost cut is beneficial.

title: Pendleton Ward: rounded characters
principle: Write characters with both strengths and faults.
keyLessons: Ward describes wanting ordinary, believable people rather than opposite stereotypes.
He describes a team writing to entertain itself. Application: try a scene that interests you, then check whether another reader understands the character.

title: Pendleton Ward: a workplace that supports play
principle: Make room for curiosity across the creative process.
keyLessons: Ward recalls learning about editing, animatics and music while working for Thurop Van Orman.
He wanted his own production to retain an enjoyable atmosphere. Application: inspect one neighboring craft and try a small experiment; play is not a guarantee of commercial success.

title: Pendleton Ward: practicing kindness
principle: Treat kindness as something to practice.
keyLessons: Ward says he selected conversations about practicing kindness and facing mortality.
Application: choose one manageable kind action rather than demanding a perfect emotional state. This is a creative perspective, not mental-health treatment.

title: Ricky Gervais: connection rather than a career script
principle: Make work around something you need to express.
keyLessons: In this interview, Gervais emphasizes what he wants to communicate and the strength of connection with an audience.
Application: name the observation behind a scene before optimizing its marketability. This does not justify cruelty or predict an audience response.

title: Bob Marley: music and social expression
principle: Art can carry a social concern while remaining an experience people enjoy.
keyLessons: The official estate biography describes music addressing oppression alongside dancing and enjoyment.

Application: make one concrete artistic choice that expresses the concern instead of substituting a slogan for craft. This inference is not a quoted Marley method; the estate account is not independent criticism.

title: Marie Curie: investigate an unexplained measurement
principle: An anomaly can be a question to investigate rather than noise to discard.
keyLessons: The AIP history explains that pitchblende emitted more radiation than its known uranium content accounted for, prompting investigation of another element.
Application: record the mismatch, competing explanations and a discriminating test. Do not apply hazardous historical laboratory practices.

title: Marie Curie: research and protection
principle: Scientific commitment does not require ignoring risk.
keyLessons: The historical account discusses Curie establishing laboratory protection measures and concerns about radium used by unqualified practitioners.
Application: pair a research plan with qualified safety review. Do not turn her biography into instructions for handling radioactive material.

title: WeWork: revenue narratives and obligations
principle: Test a growth narrative against the obligations behind it.
keyLessons: The SEC correspondence requested balanced disclosure of revenue backlog and noncancelable lease commitments during the proposed IPO review.
Application: compare promised growth with fixed commitments and downside cash needs. This is a risk-analysis lesson from regulatory records, not Neumann endorsing the advice.
